Both are mode settings by Lemma 4.2. We write $\mathcal{E}_{\ell}$ and $\mathcal{E}^{\Phi}_{\ell}$ for the two Evans functions; likewise, superscripts $\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}$ and $\Phi$ on $\Omega$ and $\nu$ indicate the profile. Since $\Phi=\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}\,\cdot)$ , $\Gamma_{\Phi}(r)=R_{\mathrm{c}}^{-2}\Gamma_{\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}r)$ , so

$$ \Omega^{\Phi}(r;G)=r^{-2}\Big(\frac{R_{\mathrm{c}}^{-2}\Gamma_{\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}r)}{2\pi}+G\Big)=(R_{\mathrm{c}}r)^{-2}\Big(\frac{\Gamma_{\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}r)}{2\pi}+R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G\Big)=\Omega^{\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}r;R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G), $$

and $\nu^{\Phi}(\xi)=\nu^{\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}}(\xi+\xi_{R})$ , as $R_{\mathrm{c}}=e^{\xi_{R}}$ . Hence the Rayleigh potential for $(\Phi,G)$ at $\xi$ is the one for $(\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}},R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ at $\xi+\xi_{R}$ . So if $\psi_{\ell}(\cdot;\lambda,R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ is the solution of Definition 4.4 for $(\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}},R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ , normalized at $\xi_{L}$ , then $\psi_{\ell}(\cdot+\xi_{R};\lambda,R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ is the one for $(\Phi,G)$ , normalized at $\xi_{L}-\xi_{R}$ , and the formula for the Evans function gives

$$ \mathcal{E}^{\Phi}_{\ell}(\lambda;G)=\mathcal{E}_{\ell}(\lambda;R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)\qquad(\ell\geq 1,\ \real\lambda>0,\ G\in\mathbb{R}). $$

#### Corollary 4.18.

Assume (N1) and (N2). For every $G\in[0,\frac{1}{50}]$ , the function $\mathcal{E}_{3}(\cdot;G)$ of Hypothesis 4.17 has exactly one zero $\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G)$ in $\{\real\lambda\geq\frac{9}{200}\}$ ; it is simple and $\real\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G)>\frac{211}{2500}$ .

#### Proof.

By (N1), $\mathcal{E}_{3}(\cdot;G)$ has exactly one zero $\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G)$ in $\{\real\lambda\geq\frac{9}{200}\}$ , counted with multiplicity, so this zero is simple; by (N2), $\real\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G)>\frac{211}{2500}$ . ∎

For the rest of the paper, $X^{s}$ denotes the space of $3$ -fold rotationally symmetric $w\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}^{2};\mathbb{C})$ with $\supp w\subset N=\{\frac{a}{2}\leq|y|\leq 2\}$ ; thus $X^{s}=Y^{s}_{3\mathbb{Z}}$ for the ring in ring units, and $X^{s}_{\ell}=Y^{s}_{\ell}$ for $\ell\in 3\mathbb{Z}$ . On $X^{s}$ , $L(G)$ denotes the linearization at $(\Phi,G)$ in ring units, that is, the generator of the restriction of $e^{tL}$ to $X^{s}$ ; by Lemma 4.14(2) it extends the differential operator on $X^{s+1}$ , and Lemma 4.16 describes it mode by mode.

#### Proposition 4.19.

Assume (N1)–(N3), and for $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ let $\lambda_{*}(G)=\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ be as in Corollary 4.18. Then $\real\lambda_{*}(G)>\frac{211}{2500}$ , and for every $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ and every integer $s\geq 0$ : $\spec(L_{3}(G)|_{X^{s}_{3}})\cap\{\real\lambda>\frac{9}{200}\}=\{\lambda_{*}(G)\}$ , and $\lambda_{*}(G)$ is an algebraically simple eigenvalue of $L_{3}(G)$ on $X^{s}_{3}$ ; $\spec(L_{-3}(G)|_{X^{s}_{-3}})\cap\{\real\lambda>\frac{9}{200}\}=\{\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}\}$ ; $\spec(L_{\ell}(G)|_{X^{s}_{\ell}})\cap\{\real\lambda>\frac{9}{200}\}=\emptyset$ for $\ell\in 3\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{3,-3\}$ ;

$$ \spec(L(G)|_{X^{s}})\cap\{\real\lambda>\tfrac{9}{200}\}=\{\lambda_{*}(G),\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}\}; $$

and the Riesz projection of $L(G)$ on $X^{s}$ for this set acts as the Riesz projection of $L_{3}(G)$ at $\lambda_{*}(G)$ on the mode $3$ , as the Riesz projection of $L_{-3}(G)$ at $\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}$ on the mode $-3$ , and as $0$ on the other modes.

#### Proof.

Fix $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ and $s\geq 0$ ; then $R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G\in[0,\frac{1}{50}]$ . For $\ell=\pm 3$ : by Lemma 4.7, run in the mode setting of $\Phi$ , the spectrum of $L_{\pm 3}(G)$ on $X^{s}_{\pm 3}$ in $\{\real\lambda>0\}$ consists of the zeros of $\mathcal{E}^{\Phi}_{3}(\cdot;G)$ and their conjugates respectively, all eigenvalues. By (13) and the last assertion of Lemma 4.6, $\mathcal{E}^{\Phi}_{3}(\cdot;G)$ is the function $\mathcal{E}_{3}(\cdot;R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ of Hypothesis 4.17. So by Corollary 4.18 the part of this spectrum in $\{\real\lambda\geq\frac{9}{200}\}$ is $\{\lambda_{*}(G)\}$ for $L_{3}(G)$ and $\{\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}\}$ for $L_{-3}(G)$ , where $\lambda_{*}(G)=\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ is a simple zero of $\mathcal{E}^{\Phi}_{3}(\cdot;G)$ and $\real\lambda_{*}(G)>\frac{211}{2500}$ ; and Theorem 4.8(2) shows that $\lambda_{*}(G)$ is algebraically simple on $X^{s}_{3}$ . Let $|\ell|=6$ or $|\ell|\geq 9$ , and let $\ell^{\prime}=6$ if $|\ell|=6$ and $\ell^{\prime}=9$ if $|\ell|\geq 9$ . By Lemma 4.7, every point $\lambda$ of $\spec(L_{\ell}(G)|_{X^{s}_{\ell}})$ in $\{\real\lambda>0\}$ is an eigenvalue, with an eigenfunction in $X^{s}_{\ell}=Y^{s}_{\ell}\subset Y^{0}_{\ell}$ . By Lemma 4.11(1), $\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}$ satisfies the hypothesis of Lemma 4.10, and so does $\Phi$ , as $\partial_{r}\Phi(r)=R_{\mathrm{c}}\,(\partial_{r}\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}})(R_{\mathrm{c}}r)$ ; the substitution $u=R_{\mathrm{c}}r$ shows that $Z_{\ell}$ is the same for both. By Lemma 4.10, the monotonicity of $Z_{\ell}$ (as $\ell^{\prime}\leq|\ell|$ ), Lemma 4.11(2) with $\ell^{\prime}$ in place of $\ell$ (admissible since $\ell^{\prime}d<1$ , Lemma 4.2) and (N3), $\real\lambda\leq\tfrac{1}{2}Z_{|\ell|}^{1/2}\leq\tfrac{1}{2}Z_{\ell^{\prime}}^{1/2}=\tfrac{1}{2}(Z^{a}_{\ell^{\prime}}Z^{b}_{\ell^{\prime}})^{1/2}\leq\tfrac{1}{2}\big(e^{\ell^{\prime}a_{0}}\Theta_{\ell^{\prime}}+\epsilon_{*}\big)<\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\tfrac{9}{100}$ ; and $L_{0}=0$ . This proves the mode statements. Apply Lemma 4.16 with $\mathcal{Z}=3\mathbb{Z}$ , $G_{+}=\overline{G}$ , $\gamma=\frac{9}{200}$ . Every $\lambda$ with $\real\lambda>\frac{9}{200}$ other than $\lambda_{*}(G)$ , $\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}$ is in the resolvent set of every $L_{\ell}(G)$ , hence of $L(G)$ by Lemma 4.16(3), while $\lambda_{*}(G)$ and $\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}$ are eigenvalues with eigenfunctions $g_{*}e^{3i\theta}$ and $\overline{g_{*}}e^{-3i\theta}$ , where $g_{*}=M_{\lambda_{*}(G)}k_{3}\,\psi_{3}(\log r;\lambda_{*}(G),G)$ is the eigenfunction of Lemma 4.7(2) in the mode setting of $\Phi$ . This finite set is open and closed in the spectrum, and Lemma 4.16(4) gives its Riesz projection. ∎

The next definition collects the eigendata that Part II uses. Two of them, $\beta(G)$ and $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}(G)$ , describe how a ring interacts with the other rings of the datum. Let $g$ be a real vorticity supported in a disk $\{|y|\leq\rho\}$ with $\rho<a$ , inside the ring. By the expansion following Definition 2.3, the part of its stream function in the angular modes $\pm 3$ is $-\real(\frac{1}{3}p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]\,(\bar{y})^{-3}\big)$ on the ring, and since $(\bar{y})^{-3}=r^{-3}e^{3i\theta}$ , the corresponding velocity $h$ has radial component $h\cdot\textbf{e}_{r}=-r^{-1}\partial_{\theta}\big(-\real(\frac{1}{3}p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]r^{-3}e^{3i\theta})\big)=\real(i\,p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]\,r^{-4}e^{3i\theta}\big)$ . The forcing $-h\cdot\nabla\Phi=-(h\cdot\textbf{e}_{r})\,\partial_{r}\Phi$ that this field exerts on the ring therefore has mode- $3$ part $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]\,b(r)e^{3i\theta}$ , with $b(r)=-\frac{i}{2}r^{-4}\partial_{r}\Phi(r)$ . So $be^{3i\theta}$ is the forcing of the ring, in the mode $3$ , by an interior field of unit outer moment, and $\beta(G)$ below is its component along the unstable eigenfunction. Conversely, $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}(G)$ is the outer moment of the unstable eigenfunction, which determines the field that a perturbed ring exerts on the rings outside it. In the relay of Part II, the kick that a ring gives to the next ring outward has unstable component $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]\,\beta(G)$ , where $g$ is the inner ring rescaled to the units of the outer one; near saturation the perturbation of the inner ring is a multiple of its unstable eigenfunction, so $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]$ is a multiple of $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}$ . This is why Lemma 4.23 bounds $|\beta|\,|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}|$ from below.

#### Definition 4.20.

Assume (N1)–(N3), and let $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ . With the mode setting of $\Phi$ in ring units and $\ell=3$ , let $\lambda_{*}(G)$ be as in Proposition 4.19, $g_{*}=g_{*}(G)$ and $J(G)$ as in Theorem 4.8, $n_{*}(G)=\|g_{*}e^{3i\theta}\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2})}$ , and

$$ \phi_{*}(G)=n_{*}(G)^{-1}g_{*}(r)e^{3i\theta},\qquad\sigma(G)=\real\lambda_{*}(G). $$

Let $\ell_{*}(G)$ be the functional on $X^{0}$ given by $\ell_{*}(G)(w)=n_{*}(G)\,\ell_{*}(w_{3})$ , where $w_{3}$ is the mode- $3$ profile of $w$ and $\ell_{*}$ is the functional of Theorem 4.8; so $\ell_{*}(G)(\phi_{*}(G))=1$ and $\ell_{*}(G)(\overline{\phi_{*}(G)})=0$ . The same formula defines $\ell_{*}(G)$ on $L^{2}(N)$ . Put $\beta(G)=\ell_{*}(G)\big(b\,e^{3i\theta}\big)$ with $b(r)=-\frac{i}{2}r^{-4}\partial_{r}\Phi(r)$ , $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}(G)=p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[\phi_{*}(G)]$ (Definition 2.3), let $\Pi(G)$ be the Riesz projection of Proposition 4.19, so that $\Pi(G)w=2\real(\ell_{*}(G)(w)\phi_{*}(G)\big)$ for real $w$ , and put

$$ z=\lambda_{*}(0),\qquad\sigma=\real z=\sigma(0),\qquad\sigma_{\flat}=\min_{G\in[0,\overline{G}]}\sigma(G). $$

The formula for $\Pi(G)$ follows from Proposition 4.19 and Theorem 4.8(2): on the mode $3$ the Riesz projection is $w_{3}\mapsto\ell_{*}(w_{3})g_{*}=\ell_{*}(G)(w)\,n_{*}^{-1}g_{*}$ , and for real $w$ the mode $-3$ part is the conjugate of the mode $3$ part (Lemma 4.5(2)). By the linearity of $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}$ and $\ell_{*}$ , $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}(G)=p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}/n_{*}(G)$ and $\beta(G)=n_{*}(G)\beta$ , with $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}$ and $\beta$ of Lemma 4.9 for $\Phi$ , $\ell=3$ and $\lambda_{*}=\lambda_{*}(G)$ . The minimum defining $\sigma_{\flat}$ exists by Proposition 4.21(a) below. With $M_{*}=M_{\lambda_{*}(G)}$ , the functional $\ell_{*}(G)$ on $L^{2}(N)$ is represented by the restriction to $N$ of $x\mapsto\frac{n_{*}}{2\pi\overline{J}}\,\overline{\psi_{*}(\log|x|)M_{*}(|x|)}\,e^{3i\theta}$ , which lies in $X^{0}$ , so its norms on $L^{2}(N)$ and on $X^{0}$ agree.

#### Proposition 4.21.

Assume (N1)–(N3). Then:

- (a) $G\mapsto\lambda_{*}(G)$ is continuous on $[0,\overline{G}]$ ; in particular $G\mapsto\sigma(G)$ is continuous, $\sigma_{\flat}$ is attained, and $\sigma_{\flat}>\frac{211}{2500}$ ;

- (b) the functions $G\mapsto|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}(G)|$ , $|\beta(G)|$ , $\|\ell_{*}(G)\|_{(X^{0})^{*}}$ and $\|\phi_{*}(G)\|_{H^{k}}$ ( $k\geq 0$ ) are continuous on $[0,\overline{G}]$ , and the first two are positive.

#### Proof.

(a) In reference units put $E(\lambda,G)=\mathcal{E}_{3}(\lambda;G)$ , the function of Hypothesis 4.17 by Lemma 4.6. In the Picard iteration of Lemma 4.6(1), with $G\in[0,\frac{1}{50}]$ as a parameter, the iterates are continuous in $(\xi,\lambda,G)$ and holomorphic in $\lambda$ , and the bound $C_{A}$ does not depend on $G$ , by Lemma 4.5(3). So $E$ is continuous on $\{\real\lambda>0\}\times[0,\frac{1}{50}]$ and holomorphic in $\lambda$ , and $\partial_{\lambda}E$ is continuous there by Cauchy’s formula. Fix $G_{0}\in[0,\frac{1}{50}]$ and the simple zero $\lambda_{0}=\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G_{0})$ (the eigenvalue in reference units of Corollary 4.18, the superscript $\mathrm{c}$ referring to $\overline{\omega}_{\mathrm{c}}$ ; in ring units $\lambda_{*}(G)=\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ ) of $E(\cdot,G_{0})$ , let $\delta_{1}>0$ be such that $\{|\lambda-\lambda_{0}|\leq\delta_{1}\}\subset\{\real\lambda>\frac{9}{200}\}$ contains no other zero of $E(\cdot,G_{0})$ , and let $0<\delta<\delta_{1}$ . By continuity and compactness there is $\epsilon>0$ with $E\neq 0$ on $\{|\lambda-\lambda_{0}|=\delta\}\times I_{\epsilon}$ , where $I_{\epsilon}=\{G\in[0,\frac{1}{50}]:|G-G_{0}|<\epsilon\}$ . On the interval $I_{\epsilon}$ the number of zeros $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|\lambda-\lambda_{0}|=\delta}\partial_{\lambda}E/E\differential\lambda$ of $E(\cdot,G)$ in the disk is continuous, integer-valued and $1$ at $G_{0}$ , hence $1$ . This zero lies in $\{\real\lambda>\frac{9}{200}\}$ , so it is $\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G)$ by (N1), and $|\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(G)-\lambda_{0}|<\delta$ for $G\in I_{\epsilon}$ . So $\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}$ is continuous on $[0,\frac{1}{50}]$ , and (a) follows from $\lambda_{*}(G)=\lambda_{*}^{\mathrm{c}}(R_{\mathrm{c}}^{2}G)$ , $\sigma(G)>\frac{211}{2500}$ (Proposition 4.19) and the compactness of $[0,\overline{G}]$ .

(b) In ring units, let $\psi(\xi;\lambda,G)$ be the solution of Definition 4.4 for $\Phi$ , normalized at $\xi_{1}=\xi_{L}-\xi_{R}$ . By the Picard argument and the equation, $\psi$ and all its $\xi$ -derivatives are continuous in $(\xi,\lambda,G)$ . Hence $\psi_{*}(G):=\psi(\cdot;\lambda_{*}(G),G)$ and $g_{*}(G)=M_{\lambda_{*}(G)}k_{3}\psi_{*}(G)$ , supported in $[r_{1},r_{2}]=[a,1]$ , are continuous in $G$ in every $C^{k}([a,1])$ . So $n_{*}(G)$ and $J(G)=\int g_{*}\psi_{*}M_{*}r\differential r$ are continuous, $n_{*}>0$ by Lemma 4.7(2), and $J\neq 0$ by Theorem 4.8(1), as $\lambda_{*}(G)$ is a simple zero of $\mathcal{E}^{\Phi}_{3}(\cdot;G)$ (proof of Proposition 4.19). By Lemma 4.9(2) and (3) and the linearity of $p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}$ and $\ell_{*}$ , with $\xi_{2}=0$ ,

$$ p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}(G)=-\frac{6\psi_{*}(\xi_{2})}{n_{*}},\quad\beta(G)=-\frac{n_{*}\,p^{\mathrm{in}}_{3}[g_{*}e^{3i\theta}]}{6J}=\frac{e^{-3\xi_{1}}n_{*}}{J}; $$

these are continuous, and nonzero by Lemma 4.9(4). Also $\|\phi_{*}(G)\|_{H^{k}}$ is continuous, as $g_{*}(G)$ is continuous in $C^{k}([a,1])$ and $n_{*}>0$ , and so is $\|\ell_{*}(G)\|_{(X^{0})^{*}}=\frac{n_{*}}{2\pi|J|}\|\psi_{*}(\log|x|)M_{*}(|x|)\|_{L^{2}(N)}$ , by the representation after Definition 4.20. ∎

#### Proposition 4.22.

Assume (N1)–(N3). Let $s\geq 0$ be an integer and $\sigma^{\prime}\in(\frac{9}{200},\sigma_{\flat})$ . There is $C_{S}=C_{S}(s,\sigma^{\prime})$ , depending only on $s$ , $\sigma^{\prime}$ and the ring, such that for every $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ and $t\geq 0$ :

$$ \begin{gathered}\|e^{tL(G)}(1-\Pi(G))\|_{X^{s}\to X^{s}}\leq C_{S}e^{\sigma^{\prime}t},\qquad\|\Pi(G)\|_{X^{s}\to X^{s}}\leq C_{S},\\
\|e^{tL(G)}\|_{X^{s}\to X^{s}}\leq C_{S}e^{\sigma(G)t},\end{gathered} $$

and, for real $w\in X^{s}$ and for $w\in X^{0}$ respectively,

$$ e^{tL(G)}\Pi(G)w=2\real(\ell_{*}(G)(w)e^{\lambda_{*}(G)t}\phi_{*}(G)\big),\qquad\ell_{*}(G)(e^{tL(G)}w)=e^{\lambda_{*}(G)t}\ell_{*}(G)(w). $$

#### Proof.

We use the setting of $\Phi$ in ring units, with $G_{+}=\overline{G}$ . By Lemma 4.14(3), Proposition 4.19 and Lemma 4.12 (which costs the factor $(C^{\rm eq}_{s}/c^{\rm eq}_{s})^{1/2}$ ), it suffices to bound $\|\exp(t\Lsec{\ell})(1-\Pi_{\ell})\|_{s,\ell\to s,\ell}$ uniformly in $\ell\in 3\mathbb{Z}$ and $G$ , where $\Pi_{\pm 3}$ are the mode Riesz projections and $\Pi_{\ell}=0$ otherwise. For the fixed $\sigma^{\prime}$ , let $\mathcal{M}_{\sigma^{\prime}}$ be the number $\mathcal{M}_{\gamma}$ of Proposition 4.15 with $\gamma=\sigma^{\prime}$ , and let $\mathcal{M}_{0}=\max\{\mathcal{M}_{\sigma^{\prime}},4\}$ be the larger of the two numbers $\mathcal{M}_{\sigma^{\prime}}$ and $4$ ; the $4$ ensures that $|\ell|\geq\mathcal{M}_{0}$ excludes the modes $\pm 3$ . For $|\ell|\geq\mathcal{M}_{0}$ (so $\Pi_{\ell}=0$ ) that proposition gives the bound $2C_{s}c_{s}(\sigma^{\prime})e^{\sigma^{\prime}t}$ , and $\exp(t\Lsec{0})=1$ . For the finitely many $\ell\in 3\mathbb{Z}$ with $0<|\ell|<\mathcal{M}_{0}$ , $L_{\ell}(G)=L_{\ell}(0)-i\ell Gr^{-2}$ is bounded and affine in $G$ , so $R_{*}:=1+\max_{0<|\ell|<\mathcal{M}_{0}}\sup_{G\in[0,\overline{G}]}\|L_{\ell}(G)\|_{s,\ell}<\infty$ . Fix $\sigma^{\prime\prime}\in(\frac{9}{200},\sigma^{\prime})$ and let $\Gamma$ be the boundary of $[-R_{*},\sigma^{\prime\prime}]\times[-R_{*},R_{*}]$ . By Proposition 4.19, the spectrum of $L_{\ell}(G)$ in $\{\real\lambda\geq\sigma^{\prime\prime}\}$ is empty, or $\{\lambda_{*}(G)\}$ for $\ell=3$ , or $\{\overline{\lambda_{*}(G)}\}$ for $\ell=-3$ , with $\real\lambda_{*}(G)\geq\sigma_{\flat}>\sigma^{\prime\prime}$ ; the rest lies in $\{|\lambda|<R_{*},\ \real\lambda<\sigma^{\prime\prime}\}$ , inside $\Gamma$ . So $\Gamma$ lies in the resolvent set. For a bounded operator $A$ and $\varrho>\|A\|$ , $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|\lambda|=\varrho}e^{t\lambda}(\lambda-A)^{-1}\differential\lambda=e^{tA}$ by the Neumann series; take $A=L_{\ell}(G)$ , $\varrho=2R_{*}$ , so that the circle encloses $\Gamma$ . By Cauchy’s theorem the circle may be replaced by $\Gamma$ and a small circle around the eigenvalue outside $\Gamma$ , if any; on the range of the rank-one projection $\Pi_{\pm 3}$ the resolvent is $(\lambda-\lambda_{*})^{-1}$ (or its conjugate), and on the range of $1-\Pi_{\pm 3}$ it is holomorphic near $\lambda_{*}$ . Hence

$$ \exp(t\Lsec{\ell})(1-\Pi_{\ell})=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{\Gamma}e^{t\lambda}(\lambda-L_{\ell}(G))^{-1}\differential\lambda, $$

of norm at most $\frac{|\Gamma|}{2\pi}e^{\sigma^{\prime\prime}t}\sup_{\Gamma}\|(\lambda-L_{\ell}(G))^{-1}\|_{s,\ell}$ , and the supremum over $\Gamma\times[0,\overline{G}]$ and $0<|\ell|<\mathcal{M}_{0}$ is finite because inversion is continuous on invertible operators and $\Gamma\times[0,\overline{G}]$ is compact. This gives the first bound.

Since $\Pi_{3}g=\ell_{*}(g)g_{*}$ , the norm $\|\Pi(G)\|_{X^{s}\to X^{s}}$ is at most $C\|\ell_{*}(G)\|_{(X^{0})^{*}}\|\phi_{*}(G)\|_{H^{s}}$ , which is bounded on $[0,\overline{G}]$ by Proposition 4.21(b). The mode- $3$ part of $e^{tL}\Pi w$ is $\exp(t\Lsec{3})\ell_{*}(w_{3})g_{*}=e^{\lambda_{*}t}\ell_{*}(w_{3})g_{*}$ , and for real $w$ the mode $-3$ part is its conjugate (Lemma 4.5(2)); this gives the formula, and for complex $w$ the bound $\|e^{tL}\Pi\|_{X^{s}\to X^{s}}\leq Ce^{\sigma(G)t}$ , so the third bound follows as $\sigma^{\prime}<\sigma_{\flat}\leq\sigma(G)$ . Finally $\ell_{*}(G)(e^{tL}w)=n_{*}\ell_{*}(\exp(t\Lsec{3})w_{3})=e^{\lambda_{*}t}\ell_{*}(G)(w)$ by Lemma 4.14(3) and Lemma 4.9(1). The constants depend only on $s$ , $\sigma^{\prime}$ and the ring. ∎

#### Lemma 4.23.

Assume (N1)–(N3). Here $\Phi$ is the ring in ring units (Definition 4.1), $N$ and $N^{\prime}$ are the annuli of Section 4.1, and all maxima and minima are taken over $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ ; they are attained, since the functions involved are continuous on this compact interval (Proposition 4.21).

- (1) The constants

$$ c_{N}=\min|\beta|\cdot\min|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}|,\qquad C_{N}=\max|\beta|\cdot\max|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}|,\qquad c_{\mathrm{out}}=2\pi\min|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}| $$

satisfy $0<c_{N}\leq C_{N}<\infty$ and $c_{\mathrm{out}}>0$ .

- (2) The number $\|\ell_{*}\|:=\max_{G}\|\ell_{*}(G)\|_{(X^{0})^{*}}$ is finite, and so is $\max_{G}\|\phi_{*}(G)\|_{H^{k}}$ for every integer $k\geq 0$ .

- (3) Put

$$ \begin{gathered}C_{\ell_{*}}=\|\ell_{*}\|\,\|\nabla\Phi\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2})},\qquad C_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}},\\ C_{\nabla}(k)=2^{k}\Big(\frac{(k+1)(k+2)}{2}\Big)^{1/2}\|\Phi\|_{H^{k+1}}\qquad(k\geq 0),\end{gathered} $$

with the norms of $C^{k}(N^{\prime})$ and $H^{k}$ fixed in Section 2. Then for every $G\in[0,\overline{G}]$ , every integer $k\geq 0$ , every vector field $h\in C^{k}(N^{\prime};\mathbb{R}^{2})$ and every $g\in L^{2}(N)$ ,

$$ \begin{gathered}|\ell_{*}(G)(-h\cdot\nabla\Phi)|\leq C_{\ell_{*}}\|h\|_{C^{0}(N^{\prime})},\qquad|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]|\leq C_{\mathrm{p}}\|g\|_{L^{2}(N)},\\ \|h\cdot\nabla\Phi\|_{H^{k}}\leq C_{\nabla}(k)\|h\|_{C^{k}(N^{\prime})}.\end{gathered} $$

None of these constants depends on $G$ ; $C_{\ell_{*}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{p}}$ do not depend on $k$ , while $C_{\nabla}(k)$ does.

#### Proof.

(1), (2) By Proposition 4.21(b), $|\beta|$ , $|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}|$ , $\|\ell_{*}(G)\|_{(X^{0})^{*}}$ and $\|\phi_{*}(G)\|_{H^{k}}$ are continuous on $[0,\overline{G}]$ , and $|\beta|$ , $|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{*}|$ are positive. Continuous functions on the compact interval $[0,\overline{G}]$ attain their extrema; this gives $c_{N}>0$ , $C_{N}<\infty$ , $c_{\mathrm{out}}>0$ , $\|\ell_{*}\|<\infty$ and the bound on $\|\phi_{*}\|_{H^{k}}$ .

(3) Since $\supp\Phi\subset\{a\leq|y|\leq 1\}\subset N$ ,

$$ |\ell_{*}(G)(-h\cdot\nabla\Phi)|\leq\|\ell_{*}\|\,\|h\cdot\nabla\Phi\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2})}\leq\|\ell_{*}\|\,\|\nabla\Phi\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2})}\|h\|_{C^{0}(N^{\prime})}. $$

Next, $|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]|\leq\frac{1}{2\pi}\|g\|_{L^{2}(N)}\||y|^{3}\|_{L^{2}(N)}$ and $\||y|^{3}\|^{2}_{L^{2}(N)}=2\pi\int_{a/2}^{2}r^{7}\differential r\leq 2\pi\cdot 2^{8}/8=64\pi$ , so $|p^{\mathrm{out}}_{3}[g]|\leq\frac{8\sqrt{\pi}}{2\pi}\|g\|_{L^{2}(N)}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}}\|g\|_{L^{2}(N)}$ . Finally, for $|\alpha|\leq k$ , since $\nabla\Phi$ is supported in $N^{\prime}$ and $|\partial^{\beta}h|\leq\|h\|_{C^{k}(N^{\prime})}$ there for $|\beta|\leq k$ , the Leibniz rule and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$ give

$$ \|\partial^{\alpha}(h\cdot\nabla\Phi)\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2})}\leq\sum_{\beta\leq\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}\sup_{N^{\prime}}|\partial^{\beta}h|\,\big\||\partial^{\alpha-\beta}\nabla\Phi|\big\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{2})}\leq 2^{|\alpha|}\|h\|_{C^{k}(N^{\prime})}\|\Phi\|_{H^{k+1}}; $$

summing the squares over the $(k+1)(k+2)/2$ multi-indices gives the last inequality. ∎
